description:
FOUND s492 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the everyday-Perl battery (#1994, b2-24).  PRE-EXISTING on main 268d7e00.  Probes vs perl 5.40.3: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/fhscope1.pl (six rows, ALL wrong), fhexit1.pl (at EXIT every unclosed handle IS flushed -- sub/block/top-level/bareword all have their bytes -- so there is no data loss, only lateness + fd growth).
  { open(my $fh, ">", $f) or die; print $fh "scoped\n"; }  -s $f                 perl 7      PCL 0
  sub writer { open(my $o, ">", $f) or die; print $o "from sub\n"; 1 } writer(); -s $f     perl 9      PCL 0
  for my $i (1..3) { open(my $a, ">>", $f) or die; print $a "line $i\n"; }  then read back:     perl 4 lines  PCL 0
  { open(my $w, ">", $f); print $w "x" x 10; undef $w; }   -s $f                 perl 10     PCL 0      (`undef $w` and `$w = undef` close in perl)
  open(FH, ">", $f); print FH "bareword"; open(FH, "<", $f); my $got = <FH>;      perl "bareword"   PCL ""   <-- half (a), no refcount needed
"Write a file in a helper, read it in the next step" is the commonest file idiom there is, and most perl code relies on scope exit instead of close().  docs/not-supported.md documents "DESTROY is never called" (#198) but NOT this consequence for filehandles; the README does not mention it.

HALF (a) -- a bug, fix now: `p-open` (every mode, 2-arg and 3-arg, bareword and lexical) on a handle box that holds an OPEN stream closes it first (flush + close, `$?`/`$!` as perl: a re-open's implicit close does NOT set `$?` for a plain file; for a PIPE it waits and sets `$?` -- probe), the same for `opendir` on an open dirhandle, `socket`/`accept`/`pipe` into an open handle.  Also probe `undef $fh` / `$fh = undef` / `undef *FH` -- an explicit drop of the ONLY binding; perl closes; PCL can do so ONLY if no other reference can exist -- it cannot know, so these stay with half (b) unless the box is provably unshared.  Runtime-only; full sweep + companion io/ legs.

HALF (b) -- a DESIGN item (Fable designs, then an agent builds; do NOT start it from this task text alone): there is no refcount, so "last reference dropped" is not observable at run time.  Candidate: a COMPILE-TIME NON-ESCAPE licence in the Facts/Passes style -- a `my $fh` whose every use is (1) the handle slot of a core I/O builtin (open print printf say readline <$fh> eof close binmode seek tell read sysread syswrite truncate flock fileno select-4arg opendir readdir ...) or (2) a boolean/defined test, and which is never returned, assigned, captured by a closure, referenced (`\$fh`, `*$fh`), stored in a container or passed to a non-core callee, may be CLOSED when its scope exits (normal exit, `return`, `last`/`next`, a die unwinding through it).  Everything else keeps today's behaviour (closed at exit).  Costs to measure before building: how many corpus/lib/board `open(my ...)` sites qualify (the prize) vs escape (the residue); the emission shape (an unwind-protect around the declaring scope only when the licence fires -- it blocks tail-merging of that one scope; FLAG the bench rows with file I/O in a loop); string-eval inside the scope voids the licence.  The SAFE FALLBACK for an escaping handle is a finalizer -- measure whether sb-ext:finalize on the stream is worth having for fd exhaustion in long loops.  ir-spec gets the rule; not-supported.md gets the residue ("a filehandle that escapes its scope is closed at exit, not at last reference").
USER-VISIBLE either way: until (b) ships, README/STATUS should say "close your filehandles explicitly" beside the DESTROY bullet -- TELL the USER, do not edit README prose unasked.


=== HALF (b) MEASURED s494 (Fable, ENDURANCE battery Q4 + the licence census; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/q4/fdcount.pl, ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/d2006/census.pl) ===
THE FD LEAK IS REAL AND IT BITES AT THE DEFAULT LIMIT: open fds counted through /proc/self/fd -- perl 4 -> 4 -> 4; pcl 5 -> **3005** after `for (1..3000) { open(my $fh, "<", $0) or ...; my $l = <$fh>; }` -> **6005** after 3000 calls of a sub that opens a lexical and returns a line.  `opendir(my $dh, ...)` does NOT leak an fd (6005 -> 6005).  This box has `ulimit -n` = 524288, which is why no suite ever saw it; under `ulimit -n 1024` (the usual Linux soft limit; macOS: 256) the loop dies at **i=1021: Too many open files**.  `for my $file (@files) { open(my $fh, "<", $file) or die; while (<$fh>) {...} }` with no close is THE modern idiom: a script over 1,100 files dies under PCL on a stock machine.
THE LICENCE CENSUS (token-level approximation of the non-escape rule sketched above; `open(my ...)` / `opendir(my ...)` sites): the everyday corpus (122 programs) 36 sites: **29 QUALIFY (80.6 %)**, 7 escape (4 passed to a user sub, 3 unclassified shapes such as `print <$i>`); perl-tests/ 42 sites: 29 qualify (69.0 %), 8 escape (6 as an argument, 1 closure capture), 5 have a STRING EVAL in scope; lib/ 1 site, escapes (pushed onto a keep-alive list on purpose).  METHOD uses (`$fh->autoflush`, `$fh->error`) appear and need a ruling: a method call on the handle is an ESCAPE unless the licence knows the method -- start with ESCAPE.  So the compile-time licence covers about four in five everyday sites; the residue (a handle passed to a helper sub -- `process($fh)` -- is the big one) needs the FINALIZER fallback the sketch names, or stays "closed at exit".  NOT MEASURED YET: the CPAN board population (the census script takes any directory); the cost of the unwind-protect on a file-I/O bench row.

=== HALF (b): THE DESIGN (Fable, s494, 2026-09-21) -- an agent builds from THIS section; half (a) is s492b's member 5 ===
PERL'S SEMANTICS, PROBED (5.40.3; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/d2006/implicit.pl + cond.pl -- these two files ARE the acceptance table; PCL answers 0 bytes on every row today):
  * a non-escaping lexical handle is closed (and flushed) when its BLOCK exits: normal exit, `next` / `last` out of it (row 4: 21 bytes after a loop with `next`), a `die` unwinding through it (row 5), `return`;
  * the RETURN EXPRESSION is evaluated BEFORE the close: `sub w { open(my $o, ">", $f); print $o "abcdef"; return -s $f }` answers 0, and -s is 6 after the call (row 3);
  * the implicit close of a PIPE handle does NOT set `$?` (row 1: 0; the explicit close: 3) -- it still waits for the child;
  * a `my` declared in an `if` CONDITION is closed at the exit of the ENCLOSING block, not at the end of the if statement (rows 9a-9d: 0 inside the enclosing block after the `if`, 5 after it; per ITERATION when the enclosing block is a loop body);
  * a handle passed to a helper that does not keep it is closed at the CALLER's scope exit (row 6); a STORED handle (row 7), a CLOSURE-captured handle (row 10) and a RETURNED handle (row 12) stay open until the last holder goes;
  * `select($fh)` retains the handle while it is selected (row 8).

PART 1 -- THE LICENCE (compile time; covers ~4 of 5 everyday sites by the census above).
A `my $fh` DECLARED INSIDE `open(my $fh, ...)` (later: `socket` / `accept` / `pipe`; NOT `opendir` -- measured: it leaks no fd and its close is unobservable) is SCOPE-CLOSED when EVERY occurrence of the variable in its scope is one of:
  (1) the HANDLE SLOT of a core I/O builtin -- print printf say (both spellings, `print $fh LIST` and `print {$fh} LIST`), readline / `<$fh>`, eof close binmode seek tell read sysread syswrite sysseek truncate flock fileno getc write stat lstat, a filetest `-X $fh`, chmod / chown / utime on a handle;
  (2) a boolean / defined test (`if ($fh)`, `defined $fh`, `open(...) or die`);
and NONE of: `return $fh`; any assignment FROM it (`= $fh`, `||=`, list assignment); `\$fh`, `*$fh`, `*{$fh}`; an argument of ANY non-core callee, including a METHOD call ON it (`$fh->autoflush(1)` -- start with ESCAPE; a later widening may whitelist by MECHANISM, never by a module's name: rule 9a); an element of a list / hash / array constructor; interpolation into a string; `select($fh)` (RETAINS -- row 8; the census script wrongly lists it as a handle slot); an occurrence inside ANY nested sub, named or anonymous (closure capture); a STRING EVAL anywhere in the scope or in a sub nested in it (the capture alist could carry the handle); `goto &sub` in the scope.  DEFAULT DENY: an occurrence the classifier does not recognise is an ESCAPE.
WHERE IT LIVES: `Pl/VarAnnotator.pm` already owns this exact kind of proof -- the S1 (`str-buffer`) verdict is "its only writes are plain roots + `.=`, every use is a transient read, it never escapes into a retaining site".  The handle licence is a SIBLING VERDICT over the same use-classification walk (rule 11: extend the walk's vocabulary with "handle slot"; do not write a second walker -- the census script ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/d2006/census.pl is a token-level SIZING tool, not the implementation).  It is registered in `Pl/Passes.pm` as a named, facts-licensed Kind-A emission `fh-scope-close`, and because it changes OBSERVABLE behaviour (when bytes reach the file, how many fds are open) it is NOT an optimisation: it goes in `%NOT_OFF_BY_NONE` (the line-track precedent), so `PCL_OPT=none` keeps it and `Pl/t/passes-01.t`'s "runs identically" contract is untouched; `PCL_OPT=-fh-scope-close` remains the A/B switch.
THE EMISSION: directly inside the `let` that binds the (possibly RENAMED -- use the ONE resolver) variable, the scope's statements are wrapped: `(p-scope-close ($fh ...) BODY...)` = `(unwind-protect (progn BODY...) (%p-scope-close $fh) ...)`, one macro in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp, EXPORTED, in ir-spec §6 as a normative statement + one example.  `%p-scope-close` = if the box still holds an OPEN stream, the ordinary close path (flush, close, wait for a pipe's child) with `$?` and `$!` SAVED AND RESTORED around it (row 1); already closed or never opened = nothing.  unwind-protect returns the protected form's values, so the block's value -- a sub body's implicit return included -- and *wantarray* are untouched, and the return expression is evaluated before the cleanup (row 3) by construction.
THE SCOPE: the declaring BLOCK (sub body, loop body = per iteration, bare block, if / else branch).  A condition-`my` (`if (open(my $fh, ...)) {...}`, `while`, `unless`) belongs to the ENCLOSING block (rows 9a-9d) -- which is also where v2 binds it (#297: a loop / condition-HEAD `my` has its own `let`; read that before choosing the wrap point: if the head `let` is narrower than the enclosing block, the CLOSE still goes on the enclosing block's exit and needs the variable visible there -- this is the one place the design may need a hoisted binding; MEASURE how v2 scopes it first).  A FILE-LEVEL handle is not licensed: its scope ends at exit, where every handle is flushed already.
COST, to be measured by the builder before anything ships: SBCL's unwind-protect is a few instructions on the normal path, but a lexical `return-from` that crosses it becomes a real unwind -- only in licensed scopes, which do file I/O (microseconds per call), so the expectation is unmeasurable; the bench rows with file I/O in a loop are the control set, FLAG > 2 %; the 50 % compile budget (one more verdict in an existing walk).
WHAT COULD BREAK (each a probe, perl -> base -> tree): the block's VALUE (`my $n = do { open(my $fh, ...); scalar(<$fh>) }`; a sub whose last statement is the `while (<$fh>)` loop); `return <$fh>` in LIST context (the lines must be read before the close -- they are: the return expression is inside the protected form); `last` / `next` / `redo` out of a licensed loop body; a `die` inside it caught by an outer eval (the file must be complete in the handler); RE-OPEN of the same variable inside the scope (half (a) closes the first stream, the scope exit closes the last); explicit `close($fh)` before the exit (no double close, `$!` untouched); a licensed scope inside a string eval's TEXT (fine -- the eval text is its own compilation unit; the void rule is for an eval that could SEE the variable); `fork` inside the scope (the child's exit flushes its copy -- perl duplicates buffered output the same way; probe, do not fix); `local $_` / `local $/` inside (dynamic unwinding order: the close runs BEFORE the enclosing scope's `local`s are restored? perl closes at scope exit together with the restores -- probe `local $\ = "X"` + an unflushed print to see which separator the flush uses; buffered data is already formatted, so it should not matter -- confirm); tied handles and `*$fh{IO}` are ESCAPES by the glob rule.
BAR: implicit.pl rows 3 4 5 9a-9d + the fhscope1.pl six rows (= perl); ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/q4/fdcount.pl: open fds FLAT for the loop and the sub shape, and `bash -c 'ulimit -n 1024; pcl fdcount.pl'` completes; rows 6 7 8 10 12 (the ESCAPES) UNCHANGED from today -- a licence that fires on any of them is a SILENT WRONG (a handle closed under a holder); a new `Pl/t/fh-scope-close-01.t` (semantic rows + a transpile-shape row that the ESCAPE shapes emit NO `p-scope-close`); corpus-diff explained per class (expect many files: every `.t` with a lexical open in a block) + one probe per class; gen bump + the three artifacts; `tools/emission-ab.pl --ref MAIN --shapes --list lib/**/*.pm`; the FULL sweep (TOTAL exact; rows that ARRIVE explained -- expect upward movers in io-heavy files where a later step read an unflushed file); companion `io/` + `op/` legs where the shape occurs (`grep -a -l 'open(my'`), `--quick` once because the change is broad; the CPAN board by ROWS (File::Temp / File::Copy style code is full of this); gate-SET scan not needed (no refusal moves); ir-spec §6 + not-supported.md gains the RESIDUE entry below; README / STATUS's "close your filehandles explicitly" sentence is re-worded BY THE USER (propose the wording in the report, do not edit).
SIZE: one agent-day.  Stop rule: if the condition-`my` scope needs a hoisted binding that touches #297's machinery for more than an hour, ship the block-level licence WITHOUT condition-`my` sites (they then stay "closed at exit"), say so in not-supported.md, and file the rest.

PART 2 -- THE RESIDUE (a handle passed to a helper, stored, returned: ~1 in 5 everyday sites; `process($fh)` is the big one).  perl closes these at the LAST REFERENCE; PCL has no refcount, so the honest contract is "closed at exit -- or earlier, when the collector finds it".  Two cheap mechanisms, BOTH to be measured before either ships, and neither in the same batch as PART 1:
  (R1) a FINALIZER on the PERL-LEVEL handle object (the box / glob), whose closure holds the CL STREAM (not the box: a finalizer that references its own object never runs).  When the box is unreachable the stream is still alive inside the closure, so the finalizer can FLUSH and close properly -- which SBCL's own `:auto-close` cannot do for buffered output.  PRECONDITION to measure: the exit-time flush walks a registry of open handles; if that registry holds the boxes STRONGLY nothing is ever unreachable -- it must hold the STREAMS strongly and the boxes weakly.  Finalizers run in a separate thread in recent SBCL: the close must be safe against the main thread (the box is unreachable, so nobody else can be using the stream -- but `$?` / `$!` are globals: a finalizer must not touch them).
  (R2) EMFILE RETRY: when `open` fails with EMFILE / ENFILE, run a full GC + the pending finalizers once and retry.  Turns "dies at i=1021" into "one slow open per ~1000" for every shape R1 covers.  Meaningless without R1.
  not-supported.md entry (replaces the missing consequence of "DESTROY is never called"): "a filehandle that ESCAPES the block that opened it -- passed to a sub, stored, returned, captured -- is closed when the program exits or when the garbage collector reclaims it, not at its last reference; close it explicitly when another step reads the file".


=== DONE, HALF (a) ONLY (s492b, 2026-09-21) ===
SHIPPED in commit "#2006 (a): an open into a handle that already holds an OPEN stream closes it
first".  HALF (b) -- the scope-exit close of a non-escaping lexical handle -- is UNTOUCHED and stays
this task's open part (designed by Fable in s494; brief ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s494/s494h/).

THE BUG: `open(FH, ">", $f); print FH "bareword"; open(FH, "<", $f); my $got = <FH>;` read NOTHING
where perl reads "bareword" -- the second open replaced the handle's value and the first stream's
buffer was never flushed.  Same for a lexical handle and for a write-then-append-then-read sequence.

ONE HELPER, `%p-close-previous-stream`, called from the two points perl's ORDER distinguishes: the
TOP of `%p-open-impl` (perl closes BEFORE it attempts the new open, so a FAILED reopen has still
flushed -- probed: the old file is 4 bytes, not 0) and `%p-install-fh` (whose own docstring says
every opener reaches it, so socket / accept / pipe / fork-pipe / in-memory follow).  It closes only
what is demonstrably an OPEN stream or a socket: routing through %p-close-impl would have taken its
NO-HANDLE arm on every ordinary `open(my $fh, ...)` and set $! = EBADF.

`$?` IS SAVED AND RESTORED ACROSS IT, which is perl's answer and not the obvious one (probed 5.40.3,
scratch/s492b/pipeq.pl): an EXPLICIT `close` of a fork-pipe publishes the child's status, an
IMPLICIT one leaves `$?` exactly as it was.  The child is still reaped, so nothing becomes a zombie.

PROBES vs perl: scratch/s492b/reopen.pl (10 rows) -- 1,2,3,5,6 fixed, and the negatives unchanged (a
dup SOURCE stays open, a loop of `open my $fh` is unaffected, opendir into an open dirhandle still
works, a first open sets no errno).  fhscope1.pl row 6 (this task's half-(a) row) now matches perl;
rows 1-5 are half (b), deliberately untouched.
NORMATIVE: docs/ir-spec.md 7.5a.
GUARD: three rows in Pl/t/fileio-02.t (40 -> 43); rows 41-42 fail on a 5ce155cb extraction, the
negatives row passes there.
TWO PRE-EXISTING GAPS the probes turned up and did NOT cause: #2031 (`$? = N` does not stick at all
-- PCL always reports the last child's status) and `$!` after a successful open on a tty (noted in
#2031, not separately filed).
NOT TAKEN, as the brief allowed: no cheap provably-safe subset of half (b) was found to be worth
shipping here -- the licence question is a compile-time non-escape analysis, which is exactly what
the s494 design makes it.


=== DONE, PART 1 (s494h, Opus, 2026-09-28; branch worktree-agent-a451844fb870e1d21) ===
SHIPPED: block-level + condition-my + `undef $fh;` / `$fh = undef;` drop.  Runtime `p-scope-close`
(unwind-protect) + `%p-scope-close` (half (a)'s implicit close, `$?` and `$!` preserved); ir-spec Â§6.5.
The licence is a VarAnnotator verdict PER DECLARATION (a key opened at `open(my $fh, ...)`, active to the
block's end / the construct for a condition-my); per-NAME was built first and measured 11/35 perl-tests
sites -- do not go back to it.  Kind-A `fh-scope-close` in %NOT_OFF_BY_NONE; -fh-scope-close == main.
A condition-my closes at the ENCLOSING block's exit via a hidden `--pcl-fh-late--N` cell (no #297 change).
BAR: implicit.pl 1 3 4 5 + cond.pl 9a-9d + 11 + fhscope1 1-6 = perl; escapes 6 7 8 10 12 unchanged; gate
PASS 271/9219; sweep 18714 (+0); companion 1 mover (io/perlio_leaks.t 0/12 -> 12/0); EVERYDAY 102 -> 103;
fdcount under ulimit 1024: flat (base died at 1021).
COVERAGE (in-block open(my) sites closed): everyday 4/6, perl-tests 26/35, board+cpan-tests 11/106.
PART 2 NOTES (for whoever builds it): 92 of the 95 denied board sites are `use:opaque` = the handle passed
as an ARGUMENT (mostly a METHOD: `$csv->print($fh, ...)`, `$obj->parse($fh)`) -- R1's finalizer is the only
way to reach them.  `%p-scope-close` is the right close for R1's finalizer too, EXCEPT that a finalizer
thread must not touch `$?`/`$!` at all (they are globals; save/restore is not enough there).  The per-decl
key machinery (`_fh_open_decl`, `fh_active` localized per block) could also carry a future widening:
a METHOD whitelist by MECHANISM (rule 9a), never by a module name.
Diagnostics: PCL_B_DEBUG=1 prints `F-DEBUG $name line N <CLOSED|reason>` per declaration.
subject: EVERYDAY (file I/O, pre-existing): a filehandle is never closed IMPLICITLY -- (a) PLAIN BUG: `open(FH, ...)` on an ALREADY-OPEN handle does not close/flush the old stream (perl does: write, re-open for reading, read back = the data; PCL reads NOTHING); (b) a lexical `open(my $fh, ">", $f)` is not closed at SCOPE EXIT, so a file written in a block or a sub without an explicit close() is EMPTY when the same program reads it back (data lands only at exit), and a loop of such opens leaks one fd per iteration  [HALF (a) DONE s492b; HALF (b), the scope-exit close, IS THIS TASKS OPEN PART]
